name: Tank Yard v2.0.3
body:
# Tank Yard v2.0.3

The bosses have started paying attention, Axiom finally has a body worth being afraid of, and the scoreboard folds up when you're tired of seeing who's beating you. It plays with 2.0.0 and 2.0.2, so nobody has to update at the same time.

## Bosses

- **They aim now.** Bosses lead a moving tank and, just before a special, line up on where you'll be when the warning ends. A sharp turn can still slip the shot, so dodging remains a valid career.
- **Straight lines.** They drive in clean legs from one heading to the next, closing in, backing off or cutting around you, instead of drifting about.
- **They notice when you're hurt.** A wounded tank is a more attractive target than it used to be. Sorry.
- **Bastion has a cannon.** Same hull, one heavy round with a proper warning. It's lighter than the Siege Engine's, so it ruins your day rather than ending it. Once Bastion is badly hurt, explosive charges bracket the line.
- A few bosses got small buffs, mostly quicker and meaner drones.

See [Bosses and learning](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.3/docs/bosses-and-learning.md).

## Axiom Worldshaper

- Rebuilt from the hull up on the glow engine: six working cannons, a turning gold and teal astrolabe, and attacks that look like they cost something.
- All twelve attacks sit on a dock with number keys, cooldowns and tooltips.
- Holding fire walks a stream of shells across the forward cannons, and they meet at your cursor.

## Scoreboard, party and chat

- **An arrow folds the scoreboard away,** and **L** does the same. It stays how you left it.
- **Each row shows that player's tank,** in miniature, so you know what's about to happen to you.
- With the tank menu open the board shortens to clear it, and your own row stays on it however the match is going.
- **Party rows show whose mic is off.** The silence now comes with an explanation.
- **Up and Down in chat** bring back what you already said, in case it was worth saying twice.

## Arena Workshop

- **Ctrl+F finds things** by kind, group, number or what a trigger does, and steps through the results.
- Drawing, moving and resizing show live measurements, and the status bar gives the size of your selection.
- Undo and redo say what they changed and flash it on the map.
- The Check list keeps itself up to date while you work.
- Copying with nothing selected no longer empties your clipboard. It was a very efficient way to lose a clipboard.

See [the map editor guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.3/docs/map-editor.md).

## Installing and speed

- The shell installer for Linux, macOS and FreeBSD now unpacks in your cache folder rather than `/tmp`, so a small or full temporary drive no longer stops an install. If extraction still fails, your current game is left alone.
- A busy match makes about a fifth fewer memory allocations per frame. The picture is the same.

## Compatibility

Tank Yard 2.0.3 still uses **protocol 34**, so it plays with 2.0.0 and 2.0.2 clients and servers, and maps and packs carry over unchanged. Boss behavior and Axiom's cannons come from the server, so you'll see them offline and on servers running 2.0.3.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v2.0.2
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v2.0.2

Everything that glows got a second look, the Siege Engine's shell is now properly on fire, and your party can finally hear you complain from the other side of the map. It plays with 2.0.0, so nobody has to update at the same moment.

## Bosses

- **Better fireworks.** Shots, muzzle flashes, hull lights, warnings and explosions on all fourteen bosses are redrawn with the game's glow lighting, and they stay bright on dark maps.
- **The Siege Engine's round is on fire.** It burns the whole way there, drags a flame trail behind it and leaves a scorch mark where you used to be.
- **Smoother movement.** Bosses ease through turns, sidestep your shots without twitching and steer around walls instead of grinding along them. Fights last about as long as they did.
- **Health bars you can read.** Notches mark where the next phase starts, and a pale stretch shows the damage you just did.
- **Arrows to bosses off screen,** with their names and health, so you can find the fight again after a respawn. Or avoid it. Nobody's judging.
- **Parting words.** Every boss now has something to say on your death screen. None of it is nice.

## Party voice

- Everyone in a party hears each other at full volume, anywhere: across the arena, while down, in a menu or between rounds.
- A mute button with the usual microphone icon is on the party rail, in the party panel and in the match, and **M** still works. Your mic starts muted, so nobody hears you eating.
- A ring around a member's tank shows who's talking. Muting someone only mutes them for you, and they never need to find out.
- The party's leader needs 2.0.2 for this. With a 2.0.0 leader, voice works by distance as before.

See [Voice](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.2/docs/parties.md#voice).

## Arena Workshop

- **A Links view you can actually follow.** Busy channels gather at hubs, wires heading the same way run together as cables, and a key in the corner hides or shows each kind of link. Point at a hub to lift its wires out of the spaghetti.
- **Gates look like gates.** Every piece in the Gates and Circuits palettes has its own symbol.
- **Connections.** The inspector lists what a trigger sets off and what sets it off. Click a row to go there.
- **Clicks take the smallest thing under the pointer,** so a trigger sitting on a spawn region no longer needs a rescue mission.
- The layer bar opens a strip of every layer in use, and just selecting something no longer marks your map as edited.

## Graphics and speed

- **NVIDIA DLAA** has its own button in Graphics.
- A typical match now takes about half the draw calls and a twentieth of the memory allocations per frame. The picture is exactly the same, which was the point.

## Compatibility

Tank Yard 2.0.2 still uses **protocol 34**, so it plays with 2.0.0 clients and servers, and maps and packs carry over unchanged.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v2.0.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v2.0.0

The biggest update Tank Yard has had. All fourteen bosses are redrawn and fight harder, tanks are rebuilt and rebalanced, the Arena Workshop gains layers, map logic gains real gates and circuits, and parties are much better to play in. Everything in [v1.7.0](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.0/docs/releases/v1.7.0.md) is included.

## Bosses

- **New looks.** Every boss is redrawn in clean, simple shapes, each with a glowing core that brightens as it charges and pulses when it's nearly beaten.
- **Attacks you can read.** Before a special attack, a boss shows where its rounds will go: lanes for a fan, spokes for a ring and chevrons for a charge. Lances, darts, shells and charges each have their own look and glow.
- **The Siege Engine's cannon.** It winds up for 1.5 seconds and draws a red line to the first wall in its way, then fires a huge, very fast round that destroys any tank it reaches, shields included. Get off the line or behind cover. Walls stop it, spawn protection holds, and a perfect parry sends it back as a heavy shot.
- **Fights that fit the arena.** A boss's health follows how many players are in the arena and how high their levels are. It moves with them if they join or leave, keeping how hurt the boss is. Bosses with swarms launch fewer drones against fewer players, and reach their full swarm against four.
- **Shared rewards.** Everyone who hit a boss in the last minute shares its reward.
- **Smarter help.** High-level bots now join a boss fight while they're healthy enough for it, and shoot down the drones that chase them.
- A warned attack always comes, even if its target ducks behind cover.

See [Fighting bosses in 2.0](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.0/docs/bosses-and-learning.md#fighting-bosses-in-20).

## Tanks

- **21 new layouts.** Bastion, Catapult, Commodore, Cyclone Gunner, Drone Sentinel, Fabricator, Fortress Array, Gunship, Interceptor, Javelin, Monolith, Octo Sprayer, Palisade, Pinball, Quarry, Railstorm, Rotator, Spectral Guard, Starburst, Switchback and Tri-Sniper have cleaner, balanced shapes, with turrets on proper mounts.
- **Rebalanced from thousands of bot duels.** 65 tanks changed.
- **The strongest came down.** Reprisal and Railstorm deal about half the damage they did, and both fire more slowly. Reprisal also has less health and a longer ability cooldown. Mirage lost 19%, and Ranger, Capacitor, Overcharger, Catapult, Riposte, Counterguard, Sniper, Stalker and others lost up to 15%.
- **The weakest came up.** Rook, Pinball and Bastille, the weakest level-55 tanks, gained 26 to 33%: Bastille lays traps faster and Rook places turrets sooner. Machine Gun gained 15%, and Destroyer, Annihilator, Spread Shot, Fighter, Triple Shot, Octo Tank, Tri-Angle and others gained up to 9%.

## Arena Workshop

- **Layers.** Every object sits on a layer from 0 to 99. The layer bar and the **,** and **.** keys pick a layer (hold Shift to skip empty ones). Everything else fades and can't be selected, so you can reach what's underneath. Layers are only for building and never change how a map plays.
- **Reach what's stacked.** Clicking the one selected object again selects the next object under the pointer, top to bottom, and wraps round.
- **The Links view (L) shows every connection.** Busy channels and counters gather at a hub so a large circuit stays readable, and drawing it is much cheaper on low-end computers.

See [Layers](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.0/docs/map-editor.md#layers).

## Map logic

- **More gates.** Alongside All, Any, Not all, None and One, a gate can now open on an even number of true conditions (XNOR, or NOT with one condition), an odd number (parity) or most of them (majority). A trigger can check eight conditions, up from four.
- **Live gates.** **On input change** runs a trigger whenever a counter or group its conditions read changes, and **Gate to counter** writes the gate's result to a counter. Together they make gates that follow their inputs, and a chain of them settles within a tick.
- **A Circuits palette.** Ready-made live gates, sum and carry bits, latches, comparators, registers, numbers and pulses. The Gates palette adds NOT, NAND, NOR, XNOR, majority and parity.
- **Faster and larger.** **Every** can run as often as every 0.05 seconds. Each tick allows 32,768 chained actions and 262,144 condition checks, and 16,384 delayed actions can wait at once. Boards follow counters within two ticks.

See [Live gates](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.0/docs/map-editor.md#live-gates).

## Parties

- The party rail shows each member's health, turns grey when they're down, and says when someone joins or leaves.
- On a team, arrows at the edge of the screen point toward allies out of view, with their names.
- The party panel lists each member's level, what they're doing, their tank and their health.
- The leader can remove a member with **Kick**, confirmed with a second click.

See [In a match](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.0/docs/parties.md#in-a-match).

## Gatewright

- An opponent's rifts now look different from yours: crimson and amber, ringed with thorns. Your own side's stay violet and teal.
- Rounds glide through rifts instead of jumping or streaking across the arena.

## Fixes

- Clicks no longer pass through one panel to what's under it. Clicking a tank upgrade over the party icon, for example, now only picks the upgrade.
- Co-op boss waves are tougher, and grow more with the size of the party.
- A window now always draws at its own size, so it stays sharp when maximized and runs faster when it's smaller than the chosen resolution. Resolution still sets the render size in fullscreen, and Render scale works in both.

## Compatibility

Tank Yard 2.0.0 uses **protocol 34**. Update clients, servers and separate relays together; 1.7.0 uses protocol 33. Older maps and packs still open. Maps that use the new gates, more than four conditions, On input change, Gate to counter or timers under 0.25 seconds need 2.0.0.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v1.7.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v1.7.0

This version adds boards, so map makers can build control panels, keypads and whole computers out of UI. It also raises the limits on map logic, gives the Zoom view trigger more control, and fixes Gatewright's rifts. Everything in [v1.6.0](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.7.0/docs/releases/v1.6.0.md) is included.

## Boards

A Show UI widget can now be a board: a grid of up to 32 by 32 squares holding up to 128 cells.

- Cells can be labels, buttons, screens, seven-segment digits, lights or meters.
- A button sends its signal when clicked, and the player who clicked is the tank that set it off. A board stays up after a click, and each player can click up to 20 times a second.
- Buttons and lights light up from a counter, one bit of a counter, or a group while it's shown. Meters fill from a counter; tall meters fill from the bottom up.
- Every cell fills in counter fields as the counters change, so a Digits cell can show a twelve-digit number and a Screen can show a byte in binary.
- The Arena Workshop has a board designer. Click a square to add a cell, drag a cell to move it, and drag its corner to resize it. **Copy cell** numbers keys for you, **Add number keys** lays out a keypad with a free channel for each key, and **Add 8 bit lights** shows a counter's bits. Each cell has its own words, text size, alignment and colors, and the board's buttons and meters take the widget's button and bar looks.
- The logic preview shows boards over the canvas, and clicking a button there sends its signal as the test tank.
- Scripts show boards with the new `board` field of `tankyard.hud`. A click on a button raises the pack's `choice` event with the button's place in `cells`.

See [Boards](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.7.0/docs/map-editor.md#boards) in the workshop guide and the [boards tutorial](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.7.0/docs/boards-tutorial.md), which builds a switch panel that opens a vault.

## Bigger logic

- Maps have 255 counters (up from 8) and 255 signal channels (up from 32).
- Counters hold whole numbers up to ±1,073,741,823 (up from ±99,999).
- Calculate has bit math, AND, OR, XOR, shift left and shift right, and a power.
- Calculate can move its counter, or the other counter, along by another counter's value. One trigger can then work through a list of counters.
- Counter fields have formats: `{3:,}` adds commas, `{3:04}` pads with zeros, `{3:b}` and `{3:x}` show binary and hex, and `{3|2|1:4}` joins counters into one long number.
- A map can hold 4,096 triggers (up from 512) and 4,096 decor items (up from 2,048). Each tick allows 4,096 chained actions (up from 256), and 4,096 delayed actions can wait at once.
- The workshop stays quick with thousands of triggers: logic links, the loop check and the canvas arrows only look at triggers that can be linked. The Logic tab shows counters 1 to 8 and any other counter the map uses or that isn't 0.
- Packs can be larger: archives of up to 16 MiB with files of up to 4 MiB, and up to 4 MiB of game data.

See [Counters](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.7.0/docs/map-editor.md#counters).

## Zoom view

- **Hold until the next zoom** keeps a zoom until another Zoom view changes it.
- **Change over** sets how long the view takes to change, 0.1 to 10 seconds, along a curve.
- **Turn toward the area** moves the camera from the tank toward the middle of the trigger's area, up to centering it there.
- A new zoom starts from wherever the view is, so chained zooms no longer jump. A destroyed tank gets its usual view back.
- Servers now send everything a zoomed-out or turned view can show.

## Gatewright

- Fixed rifts letting a tank travel through them only once a round on maps without pads. Tanks can now use a rift pair as often as it stays open.
- Rifts have new sounds in place of the old hissing ones: a swell with bells climbing over it when a rift opens, a quick warp when something goes through, a soft pop when a rift collapses, and two low notes when a shot finds no room for one.

## Other changes

- Script boards and their cells take colors as `"#rrggbb"` or `{ r, g, b }`, like other widget fields.
- The workshop plugin helpers `editor.free_channel` and `editor.free_counter` cover all 255 channels and counters, and skip the channels of choices and board buttons and the counters in bars, cells and text.
- The workshop no longer draws a link from a motion without a group to an On arrive trigger without one.

## Compatibility

Tank Yard 1.7.0 uses **protocol 33**. Update clients, servers and separate relays together; 1.6.0 uses protocol 32. Older maps and packs still open. Maps that use boards, more than 8 counters or 32 channels, the new math, counter formats or zoom settings, or more than 512 triggers need 1.7.0.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v1.6.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v1.6.0

This version adds the Gatewright tank, lets you host your own saved maps and map packs, and adds many more ways to style UI widgets. Everything in [v1.5.2](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.6.0/docs/releases/v1.5.2.md) is included.

## Gatewright

Gatewright is a new level-55 tank. It upgrades from Switchback, Wisp, Undertow or Meteor.

- Its ability, Rift pair, has an 18-second cooldown. After you activate it, your next two shots within 8 seconds open rifts where they land: a violet entry first, then a teal exit.
- You, your teammates and any bullet that enters the entry come out of the exit, moving in the same direction at the same speed. Opponent tanks, drones, traps, mines and flag carriers can't use rifts.
- A pair stays open for 15 seconds. The two rifts open at least 216 units apart. If a shot lands where a rift can't open, such as inside a wall or too close to another rift, you get the shot back.
- Activating the ability again, dying or switching tanks closes your pair. Moving walls close any rift they cover.
- The HUD shows which rift your next shot opens and how long the pair has left. Each rift shows a field of stars that shifts as the camera moves.
- Bots don't use rifts.

See [Gatewright](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.6.0/docs/playing.md#gatewright) in the playing guide.

## Host your own maps

- The host page has a new **Change map…** button. It opens a picker with three tabs: Arenas, My maps (maps saved in the Arena Workshop) and Map packs (packs in your mods library).
- When the server starts, a saved map is packed and sent to players like any other pack map. If a saved map can't be opened, the picker says why and has buttons for the editor and the maps folder.
- **Browse for a pack…** opens your file browser to add a `.zip` pack or a pack folder's `mod.json`. A pack that still needs a review opens in Mods first.
- Saved maps and pack maps host at their own size (Arena size → Map's own). Adaptive borders are off for them, so walls stay where you placed them.

See [Choosing the map](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.6.0/docs/hosting.md#choosing-the-map).

## Widget styles

Show UI widgets and script widgets have new style options:

- Shape: rounded, square, cut corners, slanted, tag or ribbon
- Border: line, none, thick, double, dashed or corner brackets
- Fill: solid, gradient, glass, stripes, grid or dots, with an optional second color
- Lettering: clean, shadow, block, outline or glow, plus capital letters and a separate title color
- Bars: capsule, flat, thin, striped, glow or pips
- Choice buttons: capsule, box, outline or underline

The workshop has twelve preset looks: Theme, Neon, Arcade, Parchment, Terminal, Royal, Glass, Hazard, Sticker, Frost, Ember and Jungle. A look changes a widget's colors and style and keeps its text, position and choices.

Scripts use the new `tankyard.hud` fields `shape`, `border`, `fill`, `fill_color`, `lettering`, `caps`, `title_color`, `bar_style` and `buttons`. Map files only store the options a widget uses. See [modding](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.6.0/docs/modding.md#hud-widgets) and the [workshop UI guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.6.0/docs/map-editor.md#ui).

## Other changes

- When the same sound starts several times in the same instant, it now plays once at the loudest volume instead of stacking.

## Compatibility

Tank Yard 1.6.0 uses **protocol 32**. Update clients, servers and separate relays together; 1.5.0 to 1.5.2 use protocol 31. Older maps and packs still open. Maps that use the new widget styles need 1.6.0.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v1.5.2
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v1.5.2

Community servers can now host arenas where moving gates close off whole rooms. Earlier versions could accept the pack in the workshop and content tools, then reject it as “invalid game data” when starting a server.

- The server checks reachability before removing the triggers and paths that only it runs. Players receive the same collision geometry and see the doors open and close through snapshots.
- Joining clients check that geometry without mistaking closed gates for permanent walls. Coordinate, clearance, size and resource-limit checks remain in place.
- Servers still reject genuinely disconnected authored maps. Regression checks cover closed gates, malformed coordinates, oversized catalogs and the player catalog's content hash.

Everything in [v1.5.1](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.5.2/docs/releases/v1.5.1.md) is included.

## Compatibility

The wire format remains **protocol 31**. Existing 1.5.x matches stay compatible. For an arena whose gates can close off rooms, update **both the server and visiting clients to 1.5.2**; older versions may reject its map data.
